scope: Every one of28 required-test clauses in plan13.1, mapped to29 named tests with observed passes on stable/MSRV plus20 archived external gates. This audits fixture evidence, not full release completion or every normative requirement elsewhere in the plan.

items.requirement: Flat machine legal/illegal transition table and terminal/unknown event behavior.
items.assessment: Flat accepted/rejected/unhandled and terminal revision behavior are checked; application predicates remain consumer code.

items.requirement: HSM nesting, bubbling, override, guard rejection, LCA entry/exit order, internal transitions and bounded depth.
items.assessment: Explicit tree-model tests cover selection/hook/depth semantics; generated tables add varied bounded forests.

items.requirement: State-local enum data construction and no accidental mutable publication bypass.
items.assessment: Typed non-Clone state and exclusive consuming owner are checked. Core compile-fail doctests separately cover identity/borrow misuse; arbitrary interior aliases remain unsupported.

items.requirement: `MemoryMachine` atomicity on faults, resource limits, panic/unwind and staged intent failure.
items.assessment: Failure, byte/count/revision bounds, poison and destructor-unwind publication are checked with typed state/head/intent assertions.

items.requirement: Transition identity and provenance correctness independent of debug strings.
items.assessment: Typed exact record/origin comparisons do not depend on diagnostic formatting.

items.requirement: Compare a randomly generated bounded machine against an independent reference transition oracle.
items.assessment: 512 deterministic generated streams and varied table/parent inputs compare to a separate oracle; augmented fuzz varies those inputs further.

items.requirement: Accepted sequence replay yields the same state/revision and intent-plan identities as live evaluation, under pinned deterministic inputs.
items.assessment: Generated accepted-sequence replay compares exact states/revisions/records/intents under pinned tables and contexts; callback determinism is not enforced by Rust.

items.requirement: Duplicate identical event does not advance state; duplicate conflicting event never advances; stale revision never publishes.
items.assessment: Historical deduplication is a journal guarantee. MemoryMachine intentionally does not retain a durable event-ID index.

items.requirement: HSM refactor preserves flat-machine semantics when hierarchy has one active level.
items.assessment: The generated fixture compares one-level Hierarchical dispatch directly against its flat table model.

items.requirement: A history split into arbitrary pages reconstructs identically to a contiguous history, or fails on malformed boundaries.
items.assessment: All256 small-history partitions under both count/byte limits, reopened readers and a missing revision are checked. This is exhaustive for nine captured records, not arbitrary-length histories.

items.requirement: Machine v1 wire parser/golden vectors and malformed schema/payload decoding.
items.assessment: Wire raw/structured mutation and preparation fuzz targets exist; independent fixtures and unit substitution checks pass. Full current-production fuzz campaign is live.

items.requirement: Dynamic event sequences, guard errors, nested state paths, counter overflow and capacity exhaustion.
items.assessment: Augmented fuzz_machine completes three100k rounds with generated guards/paths/capacities; full multi-target campaign remains separate and live.

items.requirement: Replay under mutation of order, duplicate IDs, scope, fingerprint and event digest.
items.assessment: Unit checks cover scope/definition/digest substitution, ordering and exact recovery. Existing fuzz receipt substitutions and raw parser mutation do not establish a targeted replay oracle for every listed field/order combination; inspect and strengthen that harness before closure.

items.requirement: Cross-component intent/result substitution and authorization receipt validation.
items.assessment: Typed receipt/result/source substitution checks pass; machine task/saga/outbox fuzz targets exist. Full current-production target campaign remains open.

items.requirement: SQLite serialized machines under repeated kill/reopen cycles with an independent model oracle.
items.assessment: Three seeded growing journals undergo48 real kills per compiler, checked against arithmetic/payload/prefix expectations. libFuzzer SQLite target exercises clean reopens; this seeded process-death model is a separate fixture and not a claim of kill-guided fuzz coverage.

items.requirement: Two or more writers racing the same head: exactly one distinct accepted transition; duplicates return exact matching receipts.
items.assessment: Independent workers race the same expected head; conflicting IDs refuse and exact retained retries return matching receipts.

items.requirement: Lost ACK after committed machine transition: reconstruct exact record and still dispatch each stable intent with consistent idempotency semantics.
items.assessment: Committed record/pending source survives lost acknowledgement; receiver admission and source acknowledgement remain separately fenced.

items.requirement: Crash after external delivery but before verification: outcome remains unknown until independently reconciled; never interpreted as safely repeatable by default.
items.assessment: Delivery uncertainty remains unresolved until native/independent evidence; effectful result relay and unknown reconciliation checks retain execution authority. This does not establish exactly-once external effects.

items.requirement: Simultaneous snapshot/replay readers never see a state paired with a different accepted head.
items.assessment: Concurrent journal snapshot checks bind state/head/receipt; timeline replay/finality checks have independent semantics. Neither implies general concurrent application-state alias safety.

items.requirement: Poisoned task supervisor and stopped generation cannot be bypassed through the generic `Machine` interface.
items.assessment: Poison/reconciliation tests and inspection-only task preparation retain native admission authority; no generic commit/dispatch method is provided by PreparedDecision.

items.requirement: Old serialized saga/task/timeline fixtures from v0.4.0 match exactly and still replay with the same policy decisions.
items.assessment: The compatibility checkpoint records exactly33278 task/timeline and3136 saga observations plus source bindings. Review remains bounded to those corpora.

items.requirement: External users compile unchanged against retained reexports and canonical new examples compile on Rust 1.85.0.
items.assessment: Original clause says Rust1.85. User-approved architecture amendment raises supported MSRV to1.89 for patched SQLite. External consumers pass on1.89/1.100; no1.85 candidate compatibility is claimed.

items.requirement: Old SQLite process/task fixture DB loads under the new version; v0.4 code does not silently reinterpret machine tables.
items.assessment: Actual old-writer populated database upgrade and old-adapter refusal/backup-only rollback are recorded by the upgrade checkpoint, rather than inferred from new empty databases.

items.requirement: Existing StateChronicle signed-event conformance remains intact, including rejected forged or uncommitted evidence.
items.assessment: Pinned StateChronicle conformance and native checkpoint substitution tests cover signed-source trust boundary; no unpinned sibling checkout is substituted.

items.requirement: `no_std` and no-alloc checks on machine core; RISC-V bare-metal build.
items.assessment: Archived RISC-V core bare/serde and timeline bare/alloc builds plus allocation probes cover supported fixed-profile consumer types; no physical hardware guarantee.

items.requirement: `cargo metadata` dependency checks against exact allowlisted crate graph and external feature-matrix checks.
items.assessment: Metadata, allowlisted layer checks, external consumers and14-profile source API review cover the declared graph/profiles; feature combinations outside those profiles are not inferred.

items.requirement: Production core remains free of `std`, broker, database and runtime dependencies.
items.assessment: Portable manifest/layer checks retain core no_std and no mandatory database/runtime/broker imports; hosted facade remains separate.

items.requirement: One canonical public API; legacy ports remain discoverable without requiring downstream source renames.
items.assessment: Canonical namespace map and unchanged old consumer retain selected legacy imports. Static export binding review supplements local-item signatures; no all-downstream proof is inferred.

open: Full current-production multi-target fuzz/chaos campaign remains live; shorter CI and supplementary single-target fuzz are not replacements.
Targeted replay mutation coverage for all scope/definition/digest/order roles remains only partially supported. Receipt mutation is not automatically replay mutation.
Process-kill oracle is a seeded test supplement; clean-reopen libFuzzer target does not itself kill child processes. Preserve that distinction in release claims.
Final source/harness/package/coverage reconciliation, performance findings and detailed normative review outside13.1 remain open.

generator.scope: Recorded review commit and retained raw logs; final source changes require deliberate reconciliation.
